[NLFC.9.4] **A seed's TTL counts from the engine's first sample.** A
seed is made before the engine has sampled its clocks ([NLFC.9.1]), so there is
no reading of the monotonic clock to count a TTL from ([LTIM.2.8.4]), and the
clock's zero means nothing ([LTIM.2.8.2]). The engine therefore holds a seed's
non-zero `ttl_ns` as a duration until it takes its first sample ([LTIM.2.8.5]).
When it takes that sample, the engine **must** give each seeded entry still held
as a duration the deadline of that sample plus its `ttl_ns`. It does so before
it records the sample, before the step applies the `initial` block
([LGRA.24.3]), and before it consumes the step's input. From then on the entry
expires at its deadline, as a rule's `cache … ttl:` write does ([NSTG.2.4.2]).

So an entry restored with a remaining lifetime ([NSTG.9.1]) keeps that lifetime
from the engine's first step. Neither where the host set a mock clock before that
step ([NTST.3.3]) nor how long the integrator took between creating the engine
and its first input changes it. A clone made before the first sample holds the
same durations ([NLFC.8.1]), and its own first sample fixes its deadlines.
